answer: Unique-work provenance ledger. Each identity must submit a solved, verifiable piece of scarce physical or computational work (e.g., a distinct sensor calibration trace) recorded on an append-only ledger; duplicates are rejected at the basalt layer of the hash chain. An attacker must produce a fresh, non-replicable artifact per identity, paying real equipment and time costs. Identities that fail a ledge check—matching prior provenance—are dropped. A comet marker timestamps each entry to prevent replay.
